chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about fasting while in the city (not traveling).
He said: Three days in every month: Thursday from one week, and Wednesday from a week, and Thursday from another week.

And he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: Fasting the month of patience (Ramadan) and three days from every month remove the 'balabel' (hardness/roughness) of the chests, and fasting three days from every month is fasting for the whole time.
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is Saying: Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended days for voluntary monthly fasting in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific recommendation of fasting on the three Thursdays of each lunar month, a practice rooted in the Prophet's tradition to purify the heart from spiritual hardness (balabil al-sudur). It reinforces the concept of 'fasting of the year' by linking this monthly discipline to the Quranic principle of tenfold reward for good deeds, emphasizing its role in consistent spiritual maintenance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the Fast during the presence at home, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three days during every month – the Thursday from a week, and the Wednesday from a week, and the Thursday from another week’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Fasting a month is the patience, and three days from every month removes temptation from the chests, and Fasting three days from every month is Fasting for the whole time.
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [6:160] Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about fasting while one is at home.
The Imam answered, ‘It is three days every month. They are a Thursday of one week, Wednesday of one week and Thursday of another week.

’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, “Fasting for a month is patience. Three days of fasting of every month removes temptation. Fasting of three days of every month is (like) fasting all the time.
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, says, ‘One who does a good deed receives tenfold reward.’ [6:151]’””
